Books: POST /api/books/convert, a PDF in and its text as an EPUB out, nothing kept
books 04
ca1c6487 · 10 files
Books ticket 04 (rulings in 03). Raw application/pdf body, device token or session, household membership required. 200 is the EPUB with X-Legion-Pages; 422 scanned / unreadable, 413 too_big, 502 failed, each a {code, message} sentence for the phone to show as is. - The body is copied from request.stream to a TemporaryDirectory in 1 MiB chunks, never via request.body, whose 2.5 MB DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE check would refuse any real book. The 30 MiB cap is checked from Content-Length before a byte is read. - The converter (books/convert.py, PyMuPDF + ebooklib) runs as a child process with a 50 s timeout and no secrets in its environment, so an overrun is a 502 in words rather than gunicorn killing the worker. - Scan check first: median page under 200 non-whitespace characters. - Text rebuilt into paragraphs: lines joined, split words rejoined, paragraphs cut by a page break joined, running heads and bare page numbers in the top and bottom tenth dropped. One part per 20 pages. - One log line per request: outcome, bytes in, pages, chars, seconds. Never a title, a filename or text. - Accept is ignored, so Accept: application/epub+zip is not a DRF 406. - openapi.yaml and the web client's schema.d.ts regenerated; the refusal enum pinned as BookConvertCodeEnum. Tests: 38 in tests/test_books_convert.py, including a real conversion through the child process and end to end through the view, on PDFs generated in the test. With test_openapi_schema.py: 44 passed. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Books convert: pin PyMuPDF 1.28.2 and ebooklib 0.20, the ticket's fallback over Calibre
books 04
077bfc6e · 1 file
The image change for books ticket 04, on its own as the ticket asks. No Dockerfile text changes: both install from wheels in the existing `pip install -r requirements.txt` layer, so no apt package is added. Why not Calibre, the ticket's primary. Traced from Debian's trixie Packages index (python:3.13-slim is trixie, per docker-library's tag list): `calibre` 8.5.0+ds-1+deb13u3 with --no-install-recommends pulls 370 packages, 1105 MB installed on amd64 and 1064 MB on arm64, on top of what the image already carries (curl and postgresql-client-17 are 75 MB). The image is roughly 400 MB today, so Calibre lands it at the ~1.5 GB line the ticket names. Its largest pieces are Chromium (libqt6webenginecore6, 182 MB), LLVM 19 for Mesa, SciPy, and Debian's own python3.13 beside the image's /usr/local one. And with no Docker on this machine it could not be run headless anywhere before production. The ticket names this fallback for exactly those cases. PyMuPDF 1.28.2 (2026-08-06) rather than 2.0 (2026-10-19): four days old, and 2.0 declares numpy, onnxruntime and networkx as hard dependencies. 1.28.2 has none and ships abi3 manylinux_2_28 wheels for x86_64 and aarch64, so Cloud Run and the Oracle A1 image both install it without a compiler. lxml 6.1.3 is ebooklib's, pinned with the transitive block; six was already pinned. PyMuPDF and ebooklib are AGPL-3.0; the service's source is this public repository. Unverified until deploy: the image build itself (no Docker here). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Brief News: tie items by per-Part byte offsets, fall back to section sources in words
ai-upgrade 02
23351762 · 5 files
The first live run failed News with "no item tied to a web source". - Segment offsets are read per Part (partIndex), as UTF-8 byte offsets, and checked against the segment's own text; when they disagree the text is located instead. Save places by address, rename them, and never replace or forget silently
mapbox-nav 03
e4bf26e2 · 25 files
tag_place takes an optional address: it is looked up and the RESOLVED address plus its point are saved, and the result reads that address back. Several matches or none save nothing and say so (candidates listed); no lookup service or no connection refuses in words. Without an address the current fix is saved and reverse looked up; a failed lookup still saves by coordinates and says the address is unknown. Lookups use Android's Geocoder, not the Mapbox Search SDK: Mapbox ToS 2.7.2 forbids storing temporary geocodes, and mapbox-nav ticket 03 ruled "nothing from Mapbox is stored". PlaceGeocoder is the seam. rename_place (new) keeps coordinates and address; over the engine it is one POST that also moves place reminders, otherwise reminders move via NotesController. Refuses when the new name is taken. forget_place, and a save that would move an existing label more than 150 m, now write nothing unless confirmed, returning what would be lost (the clear_codes shape). Voice audit 2026-10-09 finding 2. Saved places screen (moved out of FleetScreen.kt) gains save by address with a match picker, replace and delete confirms, rename, and the address under each label - all through the same PlaceController calls (ADR 0035). Web revamp 15: push notifications, the client half
web-revamp 15
22cbfd4c · 108 files
The service worker is now hand-written (vite-plugin-pwa injectManifest, src/sw.ts) so it can show a notification. It keeps every rule the generated one had: skipWaiting and clientsClaim (206af39), /api/ NetworkOnly and never written to a cache, and the navigation denylist that mirrors Django's own prefixes. The precache was the same 72 entries before and after the swap. - push: shows the engine's payload as sent, with a "Turn these off" action; an unreadable payload still shows something, saying so, because a browser cancels a subscription whose pushes show nothing. - notificationclick: opens or focuses the payload page (same origin only, a window already open is reused); the action POSTs /api/push/preferences/off with the session cookie and then says what the engine said, or that nothing was changed, never before the engine answered. - All of it is plain functions in lib/push-sw.ts, tested without a worker. - /settings/notifications: the iOS three-step install card when not standalone (checked before asking the browser, since Safari tabs have no PushManager), "Notifications are not set up on this server." when the engine has no keys, its own sentence for a denied permission, subscribe and unsubscribe (the engine is told first on the way off, and the browser undoes its own subscription if the engine refuses on the way on), three kind switches, the morning time, and a master off. The copy is held to the compulsion test by a vitest over every string and over what renders. - Devices now says "Last seen", not "last used": any request counts, the phone's background sync included (research note docs/design/settings-notifications-devices.md). Tests: 491 (434 before this commit, 378 before 05), from vitest's JSON reporter. `npm run push-sw` drives the BUILT sw.js in real Chromium: it activates, shows a push delivered through the DevTools protocol, handles "Turn these off" against the fake engine, and never caches /api/. Shots kept under .scratch/web-revamp/research/shots/15/. Owed on live (Kevin): VAPID keys, the schedule installed, Mia subscribing on her iPhone, a real push arriving. A row may be private to one member, enforced on the engine (web-revamp 06)
web-revamp 06
ed3542ee · 32 files
ADR 0052 built. events and checklists gain owner_user_id (null is shared) and created_by_id; checklist_items gains created_by_id. Both are set from the request, never from a body, and never go on the wire: the serializers render visibility shared|private instead. - household.tenancy.visible() is the choke point: scoped() plus the member filter, with items, ticks and skips joining through their parent. Every read and write path for the five tables uses it: api/events.py, checklists/views.py, api/changes.py and the MCP list tools (MCP writes already run the routed views). Another member's private row is a 404. - List routes and the changes feed carry a row private to someone else as a redacted tombstone (id, deleted_at, updated_at, redacted), so a replica that held it while shared drops it. Items and ticks also tombstone when their parent turned private, using the later of the two instants. - Who may change: owner may share; a shared row may be made private by its creator, or by anyone when no creator is recorded; otherwise 403 "Only the person who added this can make it private." - Removing a member tombstones their private rows in the same transaction and keeps them private. - The database refuses an owner who is not a member of the row's household. Trigger, not the ticket's composite FK: a composite FK would null the owner on member removal and turn their tombstones into shared full rows in the feed. - source_credentials.user (backfilled to a household's single owner), set by whoever hands a session over; upsert_canvas_task takes p_owner_user and inserts Canvas rows private to that member. Existing rows untouched. - manage.py make_private --origin-prefix / --structured-meta-key, dry run, idempotent. - test_visibility.py, tenancy wire check extended to owner_user_id and created_by_id, canvas poll privacy tests. OpenAPI and schema.d.ts regenerated. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

engine-mcp 10: /mcp inside Django, an 11-tool registry, read and write, off by default
engine-mcp 10
134144eb · 18 files
The engine answers MCP at /mcp on the official SDK (mcp==2.2.0, pinned with its transitive deps), driven once per request from the WSGI view: stateless, JSON responses, no session id. Tools run on the request thread, so they use the request's own DB connection. - Off unless LEGION_MCP=on; off answers 404 in words. - Device tokens only; a read-scoped token is refused by every write tool in words, and again by IsHouseholdMember inside the dispatched view. - Writes resolve and call the routed REST view, so serializers, tenancy and the gate's 405 are the REST ones. Gated tables unwritable, memory tables excluded, no ingestion tool, no mail. - Every failure is isError with words; reads say provenance and estimates in words; empty is distinguished from unreadable. - Throttled per token (LEGION_MCP_RATE, default 60/min); every call audited in public.mcp_calls (token, method, tool, outcome; never arguments or results), listed in TENANT_TABLES. - The tenancy leak test covers every tool from both households. Server suite: 1249 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 44 skipped (JUnit XML). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
